title.narrative: AAU & JU 2016-2025, CSO leadership training Commission education

description.narrative: Projektet har ansökt om finansiering från Sida om 28 miljoner för att genomföra programmet "AAU uppdragsutbildningsprogram". Insatsen avser utveckla och leverera ett femårigt kapacitets-uppbyggnads program för chefer och mellanchefer inom etiopiska civila samhällsorganisationer, genom ett uppdragsutbildningsprogram inom AAU/JU. Insatsen är relevant i förhållande till den svenska regeringens strategier för Etiopien 2016-2020 samt för forskningssamarbetet och strategin för forskning inom utvecklingssamarbete 2015-2021. AAU samarbetar med Jönköpings Universitet (JU), och en del av de begärda medlen kommer att gå till JU. AAU har varit en Sida-partner under en lång tid och de uppfyller lagkravet för att ingå avtal. Organisationen har intern kapacitet att hantera projektet.

The project introduces a Commission Education scheme with Addis Ababa University which serves primarily the civil society organisations operating in Ethiopia through provision of tailor made professional and skills training.

The overall objective of the program is to increase the capacity of AAU and Ethiopian civil society organisation to cooperate and exchange experience with partners in the Ethiopian society. The project had two specific objectives to contribute to the realisation of the overall objective.
These are; 1. To increase the capacity at AAU to meet Ethiopian development priorities by providing tailor-made services to private/public and civil society organisation active in Ethiopia. In the last phase of the project (July 2023-December 2024), this objective was broadened to include leadership training of the faculty members at the School of economics and AAU at large. 2. To increase the capacity among leaders in Ethiopian civil society organisations to further develop and sustain the CSOs through a more reflective, inclusive, and participatory leadership practice.
CED's leadership program is different from conventional management training programs, that have been rather focusing on technical aspects of running the organization such as book keeping, project planning and monitoring. CED's program aims are to go beyond the technical aspects towards a transformational mode, through the fostering of creative, motivated, and dynamic leaders who in turn manage staff (that produce the expected outputs and outcomes) efficiently and effectively from a human rights-based approach.
The methodology produces the expected outcomes and outputs.

The result achieved under the relation of the objectives of the intervention:
- Leadership Training for AAU Middle-Level Managers: Conducted in three rounds for deans and directors, focusing on leadership, change management, resource mobilization, and financial management. Enhanced AAUs ability to manage autonomy and lead institutional reforms.
- Capacity Building for Researchers (Management Staff & PhD Students): Training on scientific writing, research ethics, leadership, and data analysis. Improved research quality and leadership skills among AAU faculty.
Evidence from Review meetings, conference and closing ceremony:
- Participants demonstrated improved confidence and leadership skills during discussions.
- AAU managers shared practical examples of applying resource mobilization strategies and governance reforms.
- Faculty members reported enhanced collaboration and research output.
- Closing ceremony testimonials highlighted AAU's strengthened institutional autonomy and capacity to deliver development oriented services.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
